This picks up from a reviewed fix on the `<KEY>` branch: the review in `.repro/<KEY>/review.md` has been read and its blockers and majors addressed. The host is reached with `gh` or `glab`, whichever it uses (already logged in), and the ticket through your tracker's MCP.

`<target>` is the branch the work merges into: the target of the branch's pull request when one exists (ask `gh` or `glab`, whichever your host uses), else the remote's default branch — `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, usually `origin/main`. "Pull request" means a merge request too, on GitLab.

Commit your work with clear messages, if `/prepcook-fix` left anything uncommitted. Before you push, put the branch on top of the target: `git fetch origin` then rebase onto `<target>` and re-run the tests that cover your change. If the project merges fast-forward only (most do), a branch that has fallen behind cannot be merged and a reviewer has to ask for the rebase. Resolve conflicts yourself where the intent is unambiguous; where it is not, stop and say which hunk you could not judge.

Then push the branch and open the pull request against `<target>` with `gh` or `glab`, whichever your host uses (on GitLab it is a merge request): the title from the ticket; the description in the shape Summary, Changes, Verification, and a line that closes `<KEY>` the way your tracker links them; and the reproduction as its first comment — a four-backtick block with the harness's source from the RCA's Reproduction section, read through once more for anything that looks like a credential, and the pasteable kickoff prompt from its Reproduce locally section under `<details open>`. Link the pull request on the ticket through your tracker's MCP (for Jira, a remote link); the ticket's status is your team's workflow, not this skill's. A human reviewer is assigned by the project's rules; do not approve your own.
